about.title: Paso Robles Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Paso Robles residents rely on a mix of local clinics, urgent care centers, and hospitals in San Luis Obispo County for everything from routine care to emergency treatment. Most visits go fine. Occasionally, though, a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication is mismanaged, and a patient is left dealing with harm that shouldn't have happened. California law treats these cases differently than typical injury claims — there are shorter notice windows, expert-review requirements, and caps that affect certain damages. We handle medical malpractice claims under California's MICRA framework and work directly with clients to understand how these cases operate. If you're trying to figure out whether what happened to you rises to the level of malpractice, or you're just unsure where to start, our team can help clarify your options before time limits become a problem.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Guidance Matter in Paso Robles

items.title: Strict Filing Windows
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. We can help you figure out where you stand before that window closes.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law usually requires sending the healthcare provider a 90-day notice of intent. Missing this step can delay or jeopardize a claim, so early involvement matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, California cases typically need a qualified medical expert to establish that the care fell below the accepted standard. We can help arrange this kind of review.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery in Paso Robles — does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor result by itself isn't proof of malpractice. What matters is whether the care provided fell below the accepted medical standard, which is typically established through expert review.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after treatment at a local hospital or clinic?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury and no more than three years from when it occurred, whichever comes first. There's also a required 90-day notice period before filing suit, so it's wise to talk to us as soon as you suspect something went wrong.

items.question: Are damages limited in California medical malpractice cases?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, like medical bills and lost income, generally aren't subject to that same cap — our team can walk you through how this applies to your situation.

items.question: Do you represent me directly in a malpractice case?
items.answer: Yes — we handle medical malpractice claims and work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.
